S1Result: If your pipeline splits Playwright tests across shards, the newest release can turn a green build red.
A filter that matches no tests used to pass on every shard.
On version one point six five, every shard fails. Sixteen shards. Sixteen red jobs.
Here is what changed, and what did not.
S2Setup: The suite has thirty two tests. I ran it on two Playwright versions. The old one and the new one.
Each run selects between zero and sixteen tests, and splits them across two to sixteen shards.
That is one thousand four hundred and sixty four runs. I recorded the exit code of every one.
S3Zero: Select zero tests without shards, and both versions fail with no tests found.
Add shards on the old version, and every shard passes. Sharding hid the error.
On the new version every shard fails, the same as the run without shards.
S4Empty: An empty shard is still fine. Spread one test across sixteen shards, and fifteen have nothing to run.
All of them pass on both versions. Across one hundred and eighty jobs, not one shard failed.
S5Exception: One case still slips through. Rerunning only the last failed tests, after a green run.
Without shards it fails with no tests found. With shards it runs nothing, and still exits zero.
S6Fix: So decide what an empty run means in your pipeline.
If it is normal, like a docs only pull request, add the pass with no tests flag.
If it means your filter is broken, leave the flag off. The new version will fail the build.
One caveat. The suite is small and uses no browser. Check your own pipeline before you upgrade.
S7EndCard: Every run and every number is in the public repo. The links are in the description.
